By the Court:-
1. Heard the parties.

2. This criminal miscellaneous petition has been filed invoking the jurisdiction of this Court under Section 482 Cr.P.C. with a prayer to quash the order taking cognizance dated 20.12.2019 whereby and where under cognizance has been taken under Section 420/468/471 of the Indian Penal Code inter-alia against the petitioner.
3.
The brief fact of the case is that the brother of the complainant committed forgery and cheating and has sold the ancestral property of the complainant to the petitioner.
4. It is submitted by the learned counsel for the petitioner that the only allegation against the petitioner is that the petitioner is a purchaser of the land sold by the co-accused.
It is next submitted by the learned counsel for the petitioner that the dispute between the parties is basically a civil dispute and the matter has been settled between the parties after mediation.

Drawing attention of this Court to page nos. 31 to 34 of the brief which is the copy of the mediation report, it is submitted by the Brisketu Prasad vs The State Of Jharkhand on 14 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/60660317/

sentences.text: 1 learned counsel for the petitioner that a settlement has been arrived at between the accused persons of the case who are the brothers of the complainant, with the complainant and there is no allegation of forgery against the petitioner.
Hence, it is submitted that the continuation of this criminal proceeding against the petitioner will amount to abuse of process of law.

Therefore, it is submitted that the order taking cognizance dated 20.12.2019 whereby and where under cognizance has been taken under Section 420/468/471 of the Indian Penal Code inter-alia against the petitioner be quashed and set aside.

5. The learned Addl. P.P. opposes the prayer for quashing the order taking cognizance dated 20.12.2019 whereby and where under cognizance has been taken under Section 420/468/471 of the Indian Penal Code inter-alia against the petitioner.

6. Having heard the submissions made at the Bar and after going through the materials in the record, it is pertinent to mention here that there is absolutely no allegation against the petitioner that the petitioner has ever deceived or induced the complainant to part with any property nor there is any allegation against the petitioner of having committed forgery.

The undisputed fact remains that the matter has been settled between the parties and the dispute between the parties is basically a civil dispute and a joint compromise petition has been filed by the parties in the court of learned Sessions Judge, Bokaro as is evident from the copy of the certified copy of the joint compromise petition filed by the parties before the Sessions Judge, Bokaro in A.B.P. No. 206 of 2020 dated 05.06.2020, the copy of which has been kept at page no. 25- 30 of the brief.

7. Under such circumstances, this Court is of the considered view that in view of the compromise between the parties, the chances of conviction of the petitioner is remote and bleak and thus continuation of this criminal proceeding will amount to abuse of process of law.

Therefore, this is a fit case where the order taking cognizance dated 20.12.2019 whereby and where under cognizance has been taken under Section 420/468/471 of the Indian Penal Code inter-alia against the petitioner be quashed and set aside qua the petitioner only.

8. Accordingly, the order taking cognizance dated 20.12.2019 whereby and where under cognizance has been taken under Section 420/468/471 of the Indian Penal Code inter-alia against the petitioner is quashed the set aside qua the petitioner only.

(Anil Kumar Choudhary, J.) High Court of Jharkhand, Ranchi Dated the 14th June, 2024 AFR/Sonu-Gunjan/-
